Global Configuration

Base URLs

  • Production: https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2
  • Development: http://localhost:3000/api/v2

Standard Headers

All requests should include:

Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <JWT_TOKEN>  (for protected endpoints)

Tier System

  • Free: Base user account
  • Pro (isProUser): ₹299 lifetime purchase - full feature access
  • Plus (isPlusUser): ₹59/3 months subscription - premium features
  • Lite (isLiteUser): New Plus tier replacement (in transition)

1. Signup Endpoint

Overview

The Signup endpoint creates a new user account by redeeming an invite code. It validates the code, creates the user record, marks the invite as redeemed, and generates a recovery key for emergency account access.

Endpoint Details

  • URL: /signup
  • Method: POST
  • Authentication: None (public endpoint)
  • Rate Limit: 5 requests per minute per IP

Functionality

  1. Validates invite code existence and expiration
  2. Checks for duplicate email or username
  3. Hashes password using bcrypt
  4. Creates user record in Supabase
  5. Generates 16-character recovery key
  6. Marks invite as redeemed with user ID
  7. Returns JWT token for immediate login

Request Parameters

Field Type Required Description
username string Yes Unique username (3-32 characters)
displayName string Yes User’s display name (shown in profile)
email string Yes Valid email address
password string Yes Min 8 characters
inviteCode string Yes Valid 16-char invite code
profilePicture string No Base64-encoded JPEG image (max 2MB)

Response Fields

{
  "message": "Account created successfully",
  "token": "JWT_TOKEN_HERE",
  "user": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "username": "johndoe",
    "displayName": "John Doe",
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "isProUser": false,
    "hasAdminPrivileges": false
  },
  "recoveryKey": "16_CHARACTER_KEY"
}

Usage Examples

curl -X POST https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/signup \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "username": "johndoe",
    "displayName": "John Doe",
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "password": "SecurePass123!",
    "inviteCode": "abc123def456ghi7"
  }'

$uri = "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/signup"
$headers = @{
    "Content-Type" = "application/json"
}
$body = @{
    username = "johndoe"
    displayName = "John Doe"
    email = "john@example.com"
    password = "SecurePass123!"
    inviteCode = "abc123def456ghi7"
} | ConvertTo-Json

$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method POST -Headers $headers -Body $body
Write-Output $response.token

Steps:

  1. Create new POST request to https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/signup
  2. Go to Headers tab, add Content-Type: application/json
  3. Switch to Body > raw > JSON
  4. Paste the JSON payload:
{
  "username": "johndoe",
  "displayName": "John Doe",
  "email": "john@example.com",
  "password": "SecurePass123!",
  "inviteCode": "abc123def456ghi7"
}
  1. Click Send

2. Login Endpoint

Overview

The Login endpoint handles three distinct operations: traditional username/password authentication, handoff code generation for secure cross-domain token transfer, and handoff code consumption/exchange for session establishment.

Endpoint Details

  • URL: /login
  • Method: POST
  • Authentication: None for login; Bearer token for handoff creation
  • Rate Limit: 10 requests per minute per IP (prevents brute force)

Functionality

Traditional Login Flow:

  1. Accepts username or email and password
  2. Queries user database by username or email field
  3. Compares provided password with bcrypt hash
  4. Generates JWT token valid for 30 days
  5. Creates one-time handoff code (expires in 60 seconds)
  6. Returns token and user metadata

Handoff Generation Flow:

  1. Verifies Authorization header contains valid JWT
  2. Extracts user ID from token payload
  3. Generates 32-character random handoff code
  4. Stores code with user IP, user agent, and expiration
  5. Returns code for cross-domain exchange

Handoff Exchange Flow:

  1. Accepts handoff code in request body
  2. Validates code exists and hasn’t expired
  3. Verifies requesting IP matches original
  4. Consumes code (marks as used, prevents reuse)
  5. Returns new JWT token and user data

Request Parameters

Traditional Login

{
  "username": "johndoe",
  "password": "SecurePass123!"
}

Create Handoff Code

{
  "action": "create"
}

Headers must include: Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN

Exchange Handoff Code

{
  "code": "32_CHARACTER_HANDOFF_CODE"
}

Or with explicit action:

{
  "action": "exchange",
  "handoffCode": "32_CHARACTER_HANDOFF_CODE"
}

Response Fields (Traditional Login)

{
  "message": "Login successful",
  "token": "JWT_TOKEN_HERE",
  "handoffCode": "32_CHAR_ONE_TIME_CODE",
  "user": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "username": "johndoe",
    "displayName": "John Doe",
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "hasAdminPrivileges": false,
    "isPlusUser": false,
    "profilePicture": "https://..."
  }
}

Response Fields (Handoff Exchange)

{
  "message": "Handoff successful",
  "token": "NEW_JWT_TOKEN",
  "user": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "username": "johndoe",
    "displayName": "John Doe",
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "hasAdminPrivileges": false,
    "isPlusUser": false,
    "profilePicture": "https://..."
  }
}

Usage Examples

cURL - Traditional Login

curl -X POST https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "username": "johndoe",
    "password": "SecurePass123!"
  }'

$uri = "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/login"
$headers = @{"Content-Type" = "application/json"}
$body = @{
    username = "johndoe"
    password = "SecurePass123!"
} | ConvertTo-Json

$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method POST -Headers $headers -Body $body
$token = $response.token
$userId = $response.user.id

Write-Output "Logged in: $($response.user.displayName)"
Write-Output "Token: $token"
  1. Create POST to https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/login
  2. Headers > Add Content-Type: application/json
  3. Body > raw > JSON:
{
  "username": "johndoe",
  "password": "SecurePass123!"
}
  1. Click Send

cURL - Create Handoff Code

curl -X POST https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/login \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"action": "create"}'

$uri = "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/login"
$headers = @{
    "Authorization" = "Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN"
    "Content-Type" = "application/json"
}
$body = @{"action" = "create"} | ConvertTo-Json

$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method POST -Headers $headers -Body $body
Write-Output "Handoff Code: $($response.handoffCode)"
Write-Output "Expires in: $($response.expiresIn) seconds"
  1. POST to https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/login
  2. Headers > Add Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN
  3. Body > raw > JSON:
{
  "action": "create"
}
  1. Click Send

cURL - Exchange Handoff Code

curl -X POST https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "code": "32_CHARACTER_HANDOFF_CODE"
  }'

$uri = "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/login"
$headers = @{"Content-Type" = "application/json"}
$body = @{
    code = "32_CHARACTER_HANDOFF_CODE"
} | ConvertTo-Json

$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method POST -Headers $headers -Body $body
$newToken = $response.token

Write-Output "Session transferred: $newToken"
  1. POST to https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/login
  2. Body > raw > JSON:
{
  "code": "32_CHARACTER_HANDOFF_CODE"
}
  1. Click Send

3. Password Recovery Endpoint

Overview

The Password Recovery endpoint allows users to reset their password using their registered email and 16-character recovery key. This endpoint is critical for account access restoration when passwords are forgotten.

Endpoint Details

  • URL: /auth?action=forgot-password
  • Method: POST
  • Authentication: None (recovery key serves as authentication)
  • Rate Limit: 3 requests per hour per email (brute-force protection)

Functionality

  1. Validates email exists in database
  2. Verifies recovery key matches stored key
  3. If new password provided: hashes and updates password
  4. Generates JWT token for immediate login
  5. Logs recovery attempt for security audit
  6. Returns success message with new token

Request Parameters

{
  "email": "john@example.com",
  "recoveryKey": "16_CHARACTER_KEY",
  "newPassword": "NewSecurePass123!"
}
Field Type Required Description
email string Yes Account’s registered email
recoveryKey string Yes 16-character key from signup
newPassword string No Min 8 characters. If omitted, only validates key

Response Fields

{
  "message": "Password updated successfully",
  "token": "NEW_JWT_TOKEN",
  "timestamp": "2025-02-04T10:30:00Z"
}

Or if only validating (no new password):

{
  "verified": true,
  "message": "Recovery key valid",
  "timestamp": "2025-02-04T10:30:00Z"
}

Usage Examples

# Reset Password
curl -X POST "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/auth?action=forgot-password" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "recoveryKey": "abc1def2ghi3jkl4",
    "newPassword": "NewSecurePass123!"
  }'

# Verify Recovery Key (no password change)
curl -X POST "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/auth?action=forgot-password" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "recoveryKey": "abc1def2ghi3jkl4"
  }'

$uri = "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/auth?action=forgot-password"
$headers = @{"Content-Type" = "application/json"}

# Reset Password
$body = @{
    email = "john@example.com"
    recoveryKey = "abc1def2ghi3jkl4"
    newPassword = "NewSecurePass123!"
} | ConvertTo-Json

$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method POST -Headers $headers -Body $body
Write-Output "Password reset successful!"
Write-Output "New token: $($response.token)"
  1. POST to https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/auth?action=forgot-password
  2. Headers > Add Content-Type: application/json
  3. Body > raw > JSON:
{
  "email": "john@example.com",
  "recoveryKey": "abc1def2ghi3jkl4",
  "newPassword": "NewSecurePass123!"
}
  1. Click Send

4. Admin Account Recovery

Overview

The Admin Account Recovery endpoint is a critical security tool that allows administrators to retrieve the recovery key of any user for emergency account restoration. This is used when a user cannot access their account and regular recovery methods fail.

Endpoint Details

  • URL: /auth?action=admin-recovery
  • Method: POST
  • Authentication: Required (Bearer token with admin privileges)
  • Authorization: Admin-only endpoint

Functionality

  1. Verifies Authorization header contains valid JWT
  2. Validates user has admin privileges
  3. Queries user database by email AND username
  4. Returns complete user profile including recovery key
  5. Logs admin recovery request with timestamp
  6. Returns all necessary data for account restoration

Request Parameters

{
  "email": "target@example.com",
  "username": "targetuser"
}
Field Type Required Description
email string Yes Target user’s email
username string Yes Target user’s username

Response Fields

{
  "message": "Account recovery data retrieved successfully",
  "recoveryService": "Premium Admin Account Recovery",
  "adminId": "uuid",
  "targetUser": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "username": "targetuser",
    "displayName": "Target User",
    "email": "target@example.com",
    "profilePicture": "https://...",
    "recoveryKey": "target_recovery_key",
    "hasAdminPrivileges": false,
    "isPlusUser": false,
    "createdAt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "updatedAt": "2025-02-01T12:30:00Z"
  },
  "securityNote": "This recovery includes the user's recovery key for password reset purposes",
  "timestamp": "2025-02-04T10:30:00Z"
}

Usage Examples

curl -X POST "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/auth?action=admin-recovery" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{
    "email": "target@example.com",
    "username": "targetuser"
  }'

$uri = "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/auth?action=admin-recovery"
$headers = @{
    "Content-Type" = "application/json"
    "Authorization" = "Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN"
}
$body = @{
    email = "target@example.com"
    username = "targetuser"
} | ConvertTo-Json

$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method POST -Headers $headers -Body $body
$recoveryKey = $response.targetUser.recoveryKey
Write-Output "Recovery Key: $recoveryKey"
  1. POST to https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/auth?action=admin-recovery
  2. Headers > Add Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN
  3. Body > raw > JSON:
{
  "email": "target@example.com",
  "username": "targetuser"
}

Error Responses

Status Error Cause
400 Both email and username are required Missing email or username
401 Authentication token required No Authorization header
401 Invalid or expired token Token invalid or expired
403 Admin privileges required User doesn’t have admin status
404 User not found No user with email AND username combo
500 Internal server error Database connection failure

Security Considerations

  • This endpoint requires both email AND username match (prevents targeting wrong users)
  • All recovery attempts are logged with admin ID and timestamp
  • Recovery keys should never be transmitted insecurely
  • Recommend using this only over HTTPS
  • Consider requiring additional auth factor for sensitive operations

5. Profile Endpoint

Overview

The Profile endpoint provides GET, PUT, and DELETE operations for user account management. Users can retrieve their profile, update personal information, change passwords, generate recovery keys, update profile pictures, and delete their accounts.

Endpoint Details

  • URL: /profile
  • Methods: GET, PUT, DELETE
  • Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

GET: Retrieve Profile

Functionality

  1. Validates JWT token from Authorization header
  2. Queries user record by token’s user ID
  3. Returns complete profile with tier status
  4. Exposes recovery key to authenticated user

Response Fields

{
  "user": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "username": "johndoe",
    "displayName": "John Doe",
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "profilePicture": "https://...",
    "recoveryKey": "16_CHAR_KEY",
    "hasAdminPrivileges": false,
    "isProUser": false,
    "isPlusUser": false,
    "plusExpiry": null,
    "createdAt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "updatedAt": "2025-02-01T12:30:00Z"
  }
}

PUT: Update Profile

Functionality

  1. Validates JWT token
  2. Parses update request body
  3. Validates username uniqueness if changed
  4. Verifies current password before password change
  5. Hashes new password using bcrypt
  6. Uploads profile picture to Supabase storage if provided
  7. Generates new recovery key if requested
  8. Updates all fields in database
  9. Returns updated profile

Request Parameters

{
  "username": "newusername",
  "displayName": "New Display Name",
  "currentPassword": "CurrentPass123!",
  "newPassword": "NewPass123!",
  "generateNewRecoveryKey": true,
  "profilePicture": "data:image/jpeg;base64,..."
}
Field Type Required Description
username string No New username if changing
displayName string No New display name
currentPassword string No Required if changing password or recovery key
newPassword string No New password (min 8 chars), requires currentPassword
generateNewRecoveryKey boolean No Generate new recovery key, requires currentPassword
profilePicture string No Base64 JPEG image data URL

Response Fields

{
  "message": "Profile updated successfully",
  "user": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "username": "newusername",
    "displayName": "New Display Name",
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "profilePicture": "https://...",
    "recoveryKey": "new_recovery_key",
    "hasAdminPrivileges": false,
    "isProUser": false,
    "isPlusUser": false,
    "plusExpiry": null,
    "createdAt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "updatedAt": "2025-02-04T10:30:00Z"
  }
}

DELETE: Delete Account

Functionality

  1. Validates JWT token
  2. Verifies current password in request body
  3. Deletes user record and all associated data
  4. Removes profile pictures from storage
  5. Returns success confirmation

Request Parameters

{
  "currentPassword": "CurrentPass123!"
}

Response

{
  "message": "Account deleted successfully",
  "timestamp": "2025-02-04T10:30:00Z"
}

Usage Examples

Get Profile

curl -X GET https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/profile \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN"

$uri = "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/profile"
$headers = @{"Authorization" = "Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN"}

$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method GET -Headers $headers
$profile = $response.user

Write-Output "Username: $($profile.username)"
Write-Output "Display Name: $($profile.displayName)"
Write-Output "Email: $($profile.email)"
Write-Output "Pro User: $($profile.isProUser)"
  1. GET to https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/profile
  2. Headers > Add Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN
  3. Click Send

Update Profile

curl -X PUT https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/profile \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN" \
  -d '{
    "displayName": "John Updated",
    "currentPassword": "CurrentPass123!",
    "newPassword": "NewPass123!"
  }'

$uri = "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/profile"
$headers = @{
    "Content-Type" = "application/json"
    "Authorization" = "Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN"
}
$body = @{
    displayName = "New Display Name"
    currentPassword = "CurrentPass123!"
    newPassword = "NewPass123!"
} | ConvertTo-Json

$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method PUT -Headers $headers -Body $body
Write-Output "Profile updated: $($response.user.displayName)"
  1. PUT to https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/profile
  2. Headers > Add Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN
  3. Body > raw > JSON:
{
  "displayName": "New Display Name",
  "currentPassword": "CurrentPass123!",
  "newPassword": "NewPass123!"
}

6. AI Chat Endpoint

Overview

The AI Chat endpoint provides intelligent conversational AI with support for multiple specialized modes: general conversation, reasoning/problem-solving, code generation, and image analysis. It uses OpenRouter’s API to access various AI models with free tier support.

Endpoint Details

  • URL: /chat
  • Methods: GET (list models), POST (send message)
  • Authentication: Optional (free for guest, full features require token)
  • Rate Limit: 50 requests per hour (free), 500/hour (Pro), unlimited (Plus)

Functionality

  1. Accepts message and mode parameter
  2. Selects appropriate model based on mode
  3. Maintains conversation context if session ID provided
  4. Processes request through OpenRouter API
  5. Streams or batches response based on client
  6. Applies safety filters to inappropriate content
  7. Logs usage for analytics
  8. Returns formatted response with LaTeX support

Available Modes

Mode Use Case Models
general Casual conversation, general questions Gemini 2.0, Llama, Mistral, GPT-OSS
reasoning Complex problems, logic, step-by-step DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama
code Programming, debugging, algorithms DeepSeek, Qwen Coder, Mistral
image Image analysis, vision tasks Gemini 2.0, Nemotron, Llama 4

Request Parameters

{
  "message": "Explain binary search algorithm",
  "mode": "code",
  "sessionId": "optional_session_id",
  "model": "optional_specific_model_id"
}
Field Type Required Description
message string Yes User’s question or prompt
mode string No general, reasoning, code, or image (default: general)
sessionId string No UUID to maintain conversation context
model string No Specific model ID to override default selection

Response Fields

{
  "success": true,
  "response": "Binary search is an efficient algorithm...",
  "mode": "code",
  "model": "deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3-0324:free",
  "tokensUsed": {
    "input": 45,
    "output": 250,
    "total": 295

  "timestamp": "2025-02-04T10:30:00Z"
}

GET: List Available Models

Response

7. Search Endpoint

Overview

The Search endpoint provides intelligent content discovery through a hybrid approach combining Fuse.js fuzzy string matching with optional AI fallback for complex queries. It searches through educational materials, posts, and documents with content safety filtering.

Endpoint Details

  • URL: /search
  • Method: POST
  • Authentication: Optional (better results with token)
  • Rate Limit: 30 requests per minute

Functionality

  1. Validates search query for length and appropriateness
  2. Filters unsafe/gibberish content
  3. Performs Fuse.js fuzzy search on indexed content
  4. If useAI enabled and results below threshold: queries AI
  5. Deduplicates results
  6. Ranks by relevance score
  7. Returns paginated results

Request Parameters

{
  "query": "operating system concepts",
  "useAI": true,
  "threshold": 0.4,
  "limit": 10,
  "offset": 0
}
Field Type Required Description
query string Yes Search term (1-200 characters)
useAI boolean No Enable AI fallback (default: false)
threshold number No Minimum relevance score 0-1 (default: 0.5)
limit number No Results per page (default: 10, max: 50)
offset number No Pagination offset (default: 0)

Response Fields

{
  "success": true,
  "query": "operating system",
  "resultsCount": 15,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "title": "Operating Systems Basics",
      "excerpt": "An operating system is system software...",
      "category": "Tutorials",
      "relevance": 0.95,
      "url": "/docs/os-basics"
    },
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "title": "Process Management",
      "excerpt": "Process management is a core function...",
      "category": "Chapters",
      "relevance": 0.87,
      "url": "/docs/process-management"
    }
  ],
  "searchSource": "fuzzy",
  "executionTime": 45
}

Response Fields - AI Fallback

{
  "success": true,
  "query": "operating system",
  "resultsCount": 5,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "ai_generated",
      "title": "AI Answer: Operating Systems Overview",
      "content": "An operating system (OS) is system software...",
      "category": "AI Generated",
      "relevance": 0.75,
      "timestamp": "2025-02-04T10:30:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "searchSource": "ai_fallback",
  "executionTime": 1200
}

Usage Examples

Fuzzy Search Only

    limit = 10
} | ConvertTo-Json

$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method POST -Headers $headers -Body $body
Write-Output "Found $($response.resultsCount) results"

{
  "query": "operating system",
  "threshold": 0.5
}

Search with AI Fallback

8. Features Endpoint

Overview

The Features endpoint is a multi-purpose action handler providing advanced functionality: Google Drive integration, cloud notebooks, forms system, community contributions, promos, sharelinks, insights analytics, and subscription management.

Endpoint Details

  • URL: /features?action=X
  • Method: GET, POST (varies by action)
  • Authentication: Required for most actions
  • Actions: 8+ sub-endpoints

Available Actions

Action Method Purpose
google-drive GET/POST Manage Google Drive files
notebooks GET/POST Cloud note synchronization
forms GET/POST Form creation and submission
contribute POST Upload content to CDN
save-promo POST Save promotional codes
sharelink POST Create shareable links
insights GET Real-time analytics data
subscription POST Manage Plus tier subscription

9. Invites Endpoint

Overview

The Invites endpoint manages invite code creation, validation, redemption, user privilege toggles, and administrative controls. Administrators can create invites, toggle user permissions, validate codes, and manage the invite system.

Endpoint Details

  • URL: /invites
  • Methods: GET, POST
  • Authentication: Required (admin for management)

Public Endpoints (No Auth)

Validate Invite Code

Check if invite code is valid and available.

curl -X POST "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/invites/validate" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"code": "abc123def456ghi7"}'

$uri = "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/invites/validate"
$headers = @{"Content-Type" = "application/json"}
$body = @{
    code = "abc123def456ghi7"
} | ConvertTo-Json

$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method POST -Headers $headers -Body $body
Write-Output "Valid: $($response.valid)"
Write-Output "Redeemed: $($response.redeemed)"
  1. POST to https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/invites/validate
  2. Headers: Content-Type: application/json
  3. Body > raw > JSON:
{
  "code": "abc123def456ghi7"
}

Response:

{
  "valid": true,
  "code": "abc123def456ghi7",
  "expired": false,
  "redeemed": false,
  "containsPlusPerks": true
}

Dynamic Invite

curl -X GET "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/invites?inviteCode=abc123def456ghi7"

Write-Output "Valid: $($response.valid)"
Write-Output "Redeemed: $($response.redeemed)"

Admin Endpoints (Auth Required)

Create Invites

10. CDN Management Endpoint

Overview

The CDN Management endpoint provides administrative control over static resources hosted on GitHub (cdn-materio repository). It supports file uploads, deletions, renames, and batch operations with atomic commits.

Endpoint Details

  • URL: /cdn
  • Methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE
  • Authentication: Required (admin privileges)

GET: List Files

List Root Directory

curl -X GET "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/cdn" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN"

$uri = "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/cdn"
$headers = @{"Authorization" = "Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN"}

$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method GET -Headers $headers
Write-Output "Files in root:"
foreach ($file in $response.files) {
    Write-Output "  $($file.name) ($($file.type))"
}
  1. GET to https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/cdn
  2. Headers: Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN
  3. Send the request

List Subdirectory

curl -X GET "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/cdn?path=pdfs/semester-4" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN"

$uri = "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/cdn?path=pdfs/semester-4"
$headers = @{"Authorization" = "Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN"}

$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method GET -Headers $headers
foreach ($file in $response.files) {
    Write-Output "$($file.name): $($file.url)"
}
  1. GET to https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/cdn?path=pdfs/semester-4
  2. Headers: Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN
  3. Send the request

Response:

{
  "files": [
    {
      "name": "operating-systems.pdf",
      "type": "file",
      "size": 2048576,
      "url": "https://cdn-materio.vercel.app/pdfs/semester-4/operating-systems.pdf",
      "lastModified": "2025-02-03T12:30:00Z"
    },
    {
      "name": "notes",
      "type": "directory",
      "url": "https://cdn-materio.vercel.app/pdfs/semester-4/notes/"
    }
  ]
}

POST: Upload File

Single File Upload

curl -X POST "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/cdn" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -F "path=pdfs/sem4" \
  -F "file=@/local/notes.pdf"

$uri = "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/cdn"
$filePath = "C:\notes\operating-systems.pdf"
$headers = @{"Authorization" = "Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN"}

$form = @{
    path = "pdfs/semester4"
    file = Get-Item $filePath
}

$response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method POST -Form $form `
    -Headers $headers

Write-Output "Uploaded: $($response.file.url)"
  1. POST to https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/cdn
  2. Headers: Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN
  3. Body > form-data:
    • Key: path Value: pdfs/sem4
    • Key: file Type: File Select your PDF
  4. Send the request

Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "file": {
    "name": "notes.pdf",
    "path": "pdfs/sem4/notes.pdf",
    "url": "https://cdn-materio.vercel.app/pdfs/sem4/notes.pdf",
    "size": 1024000,
    "commit": "abc123def456"
  }
}

Staged Upload (Atomic)

Upload multiple files with single commit.

Stage files:

curl -X POST "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/cdn?stage=true" \

curl -X POST "https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/cdn?commit=true" \

  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

    "message": "Add semester 4 PDFs"

Write-Output "Services:"
Write-Output "  Supabase: $($response.supabase.status) ($($response.supabase.latencyMs)ms)"
Write-Output "  CDN: $($response.cdn.status) ($($response.cdn.latencyMs)ms)"
Write-Output ""
Write-Output "System:"
Write-Output "  CPU: $($response.system.cpuUsage)%"
Write-Output "  Memory: $($response.system.memoryUsage)%"
Write-Output "  Free: $($response.system.freeMemory)"
Write-Output ""
Write-Output "Errors (Last Hour): $($response.recentErrors)"
  1. GET to https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/health
  2. Click Send
  3. Observe JSON response with all service statuses

Global HTTP Error Reference

This section consolidates all error responses across all API endpoints. Use this as a single reference for understanding error codes and how to handle them.

HTTP Status Codes and Meanings

Code Name Applicable To Action
200 OK All endpoints Request succeeded, proceed normally
201 Created Signup, Create Invites, Create Form Resource created successfully
400 Bad Request All endpoints Fix invalid input - missing fields, wrong types, validation failures
401 Unauthorized Auth endpoints, Protected endpoints Invalid/missing token, wrong credentials, expired recovery key
403 Forbidden Admin endpoints Lack admin privileges, permission denied
404 Not Found Profile, Invites, CDN, Forms Resource doesn’t exist (user, invite, file, form)
405 Method Not Allowed Auth endpoints Wrong HTTP method (GET instead of POST)
409 Conflict Signup, Invites Resource conflict - duplicate username, already redeemed invite
413 Payload Too Large Features (upload), CDN File/body exceeds size limit
429 Too Many Requests All endpoints Rate limit exceeded, exponential backoff required
500 Internal Server Error All endpoints Server-side failure - usually database issues
503 Service Unavailable Health, Search, Features External service down (Supabase, OpenRouter, GitHub)

Endpoint-Specific Errors

Signup: Missing fields, invalid email, weak password, invalid/expired invite, duplicate username/email, rate limited
Login: Missing credentials, invalid credentials, invalid/expired token, handoff code issues, rate limited
Password Recovery: Missing email/key, user not found, invalid recovery key, rate limited
Admin Recovery: Missing token/user info, invalid token, no admin privileges, user not found, rate limited
Profile: Invalid fields, weak password, no auth, wrong password, cannot modify others, user not found
Chat: Missing query, invalid model, inappropriate content, no auth, rate limited, AI service issues
Search: Missing query, query length issues, invalid threshold, inappropriate content, rate limited
Features: Missing action, invalid action, missing parameters, file too large, no auth, insufficient permissions
Invites: Invalid code format, missing parameters, no auth, no admin privileges, code not found, already redeemed
CDN: Missing path, file too large, invalid path, no auth, no admin privileges, file not found, already exists, rate limited

For detailed error responses and solutions, refer to the HTTP Status Codes section above. All endpoints follow standard HTTP error codes (400, 401, 403, 404, 429, 500, 503).

Health Check Endpoint (GET /health)

Status codes: 200 (healthy), 503 (unavailable)
Errors: Service down, components unavailable
Use this endpoint to monitor API health and component status. Returns detailed latency metrics and error tracking.

Error Handling Best Practices

For 401/403 Errors:

  • Check token exists in Authorization header
  • Verify token hasn’t expired (30-day expiration)
  • Confirm user has required admin/Plus privileges
  • Regenerate token by logging in again

For 429 Errors:

  • Implement exponential backoff: retry with increasing delays
  • Check Retry-After header if provided
  • Typical limits: 5-50 requests per minute per endpoint
  • Cache results when possible to reduce requests

For 500/503 Errors:

  • These are temporary server issues, retry with backoff
  • Check API status page: https://materioa.vercel.app/api/v2/health
  • Contact support if errors persist for 30+ minutes
  • Implement circuit breaker pattern for resilience

For 400 Errors:

  • Validate all required fields before sending request
  • Check data types match schema (string vs number)
  • Verify length constraints (usernames, passwords, etc.)
  • Ensure proper encoding for special characters

Common Error Scenarios

Missing Authentication:

{
  "error": "Authentication token required",
  "statusCode": 401
}

Invalid Token:

{
  "error": "Invalid or expired token",
  "statusCode": 401
}

Insufficient Permissions:

{
  "error": "Admin privileges required",
  "statusCode": 403
}

Validation Error:

{
  "error": "Username already taken",
  "statusCode": 409
}

Rate Limited:

{
  "error": "Rate limit exceeded. Max 50 requests per hour",
  "retryAfter": 3600,
  "statusCode": 429
}

Security Best Practices

1. Token Management

  • Never hardcode tokens in client-side code
  • Store tokens in secure, httpOnly cookies or encrypted localStorage
  • Include Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN> in all authenticated requests
  • Tokens expire after 30 days; implement refresh logic
  • Use HTTPS only for all API requests

2. Handoff Codes

  • Exchange handoff codes immediately after login (60-second expiration)
  • Use for secure cross-domain session transfer
  • One-time use only - each code can be consumed once
  • Store handoff code in memory, not localStorage
  • Verify requesting IP matches original login IP

3. Recovery Keys

  • Generate 16-character recovery keys during signup
  • Never expose recovery keys in logs or error messages
  • Advise users to store keys offline in secure location
  • Only recovery method if password is forgotten
  • Consider implementing time-based access restrictions

4. Password Security

  • Enforce minimum 8 characters
  • Recommend mixed case, numbers, special characters
  • Hash all passwords with bcrypt (minimum 10 rounds)
  • Never transmit or log plaintext passwords
  • Implement password strength indicators

5. API Security

  • CORS is enforced - only whitelisted origins accepted
  • All admin operations require authentication + privileges
  • Admin endpoints verified server-side (never client-side)
  • Rate limiting prevents brute-force attacks
  • Content safety filters detect inappropriate queries

6. Data Privacy

  • Email addresses are private - never display publicly
  • Profile pictures uploaded to secure storage (Supabase)
  • Never log sensitive data (passwords, tokens, recovery keys)
  • Implement data retention policies for inactive accounts
  • GDPR compliant account deletion available

7. Admin Operations

  • Admin tokens never exposed to frontend
  • Admin privileges verified on every request
  • Admin recovery requires both email AND username
  • Log all admin actions with timestamp/admin ID
  • Implement admin action audit trail

8. Third-party Integrations

  • Google Drive: OAuth2 with minimal scope
  • GitHub CDN: Atomic commits prevent race conditions
  • OpenRouter AI: API key never transmitted to client
  • Razorpay: Payment processing PCI-DSS compliant

9. File Uploads

  • Max file size: 6 MB
  • Validate file types server-side
  • Scan for malware before storage
  • Store in isolated cloud buckets
  • Implement virus scanning for user uploads

10. Monitoring & Logging

  • Monitor failed authentication attempts
  • Alert on suspicious admin activity
  • Log all API errors for debugging
  • Track rate limit violations
  • Monitor for DDoS patterns

API Integration Patterns

Complete Login Flow

// Step 1: Traditional Login
POST /login
{
  "username": "johndoe",
  "password": "SecurePass123!"
}

Response:
{
  "token": "JWT_TOKEN",
  "handoffCode": "HANDOFF_CODE"
}

// Step 2: Exchange Handoff Code (for cross-domain)
POST /login
{
  "code": "HANDOFF_CODE"
}

Response:
{
  "token": "NEW_JWT_TOKEN",
  "user": { ... }
}

// Step 3: Use Token for Authenticated Requests
GET /profile
Headers: Authorization: Bearer JWT_TOKEN

Complete Signup Flow

// Step 1: Validate Invite
POST /invites/validate
{
  "code": "INVITE_CODE"
}

Response:
{
  "valid": true,
  "containsPlusPerks": true
}

// Step 2: Create Account
POST /signup
{
  "username": "johndoe",
  "displayName": "John Doe",
  "email": "john@example.com",
  "password": "SecurePass123!",
  "inviteCode": "INVITE_CODE"
}

Response:
{
  "token": "JWT_TOKEN",
  "recoveryKey": "16_CHAR_KEY"
}

// Step 3: Logged In - Use Token
GET /profile
Headers: Authorization: Bearer JWT_TOKEN

AI Chat Integration

// Get available models
GET /chat/models

// Send message
POST /chat
{
  "message": "Explain REST API",
  "mode": "general"
}

// Process response
Response:
{
  "response": "A REST API is...",
  "model": "gemini-2.0-flash"
}

Admin Operations

// Create invites
POST /invites
Headers: Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN
{
  "action": "create",
  "total": 10,
  "containsPlusPerks": true
}

// Upload CDN file
POST /cdn
Headers: Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN
-F "path=pdfs/sem4"
-F "file=@notes.pdf"

// Get health status
GET /health

The Materio API v2 provides a comprehensive platform for educational technology with 11 core endpoints covering authentication, content management, AI integration, and administrative controls. All examples in this documentation are production-ready and can be directly integrated into your applications.
